slides.heading: The *Format* block
slides.voiceover: Open the Definition tab. The Format block has three fields. Data type, number of characters, and decimal places. Decimal places are the digits after the point.
slides.spoken: Open the Definition tab. The Format block has three fields. Data type, number of characters, and decimal places. Decimal places are the digits after the point.

slides.heading: Three types, *three jobs*
slides.voiceover: CHAR takes any characters, like a sales order number. NUMC takes digits only, padded with zeros, like an item number. DEC is a packed number. That's a number SAP can calculate with, decimals included.
slides.spoken: CHAR takes any characters, like a sales order number. NUMC takes digits only, padded with zeros, like an item number. DEC is a packed number. That's a number SAP can calculate with, decimals included.

slides.label: COMMON MISTAKE
slides.heading: A discount of *12.50*
slides.voiceover: Common mistake: NUMC for a discount rate. It can't hold twelve point five zero. Use DEC, with two decimal places.
slides.spoken: Common mistake: NUMC for a discount rate. It can't hold 12.50. Use DEC, with 2 decimal places.

slides.label: REMEMBER
slides.heading: Pick by *what you store*
slides.body: IDs and text: CHAR. Digits with leading zeros: NUMC. Numbers you calculate with: DEC.
slides.voiceover: Here's the takeaway. Pick the type by what you store. Not by how the data looks.
slides.spoken: Here's the takeaway. Pick the type by what you store. Not by how the data looks.

You picked the wrong data type? Here's how to tell.

SAP domain, Part 5 of 12: the Format block on the Definition tab (data type, number of characters, decimal places).

1. CHAR: letters, digits and symbols (VBELN is CHAR 10)
2. NUMC: digits only, padded with leading zeros (POSNR is NUMC 6)
3. DEC: a packed number you calculate with, including decimal places
4. Common mistake: NUMC for a value like 12.50. Use DEC with 2 decimals

slides.title: Stop saving dates as *CHAR 8*
slides.voiceover: Stop saving dates as CHAR eight. Last time we learned CHAR, NUMC and DEC. Now, dates, times and money.
slides.spoken: Stop saving dates as CHAR 8. Last time we learned CHAR, NUMC and DEC. Now, dates, times and money.

slides.label: COMMON MISTAKE
slides.heading: A date field, *two ways*
slides.voiceover: A plain CHAR eight takes any text, even thirty-two February. DATS is a real date. SAP checks it and offers a calendar.
slides.spoken: A plain CHAR 8 takes any text, even 32 February. DATS is a real date. SAP checks it and offers a calendar.

slides.heading: Dates, times, *money*
slides.voiceover: DATS stores a date, year, month, day. TIMS stores a time, hours, minutes, seconds. CURR holds an amount. QUAN holds a quantity.
slides.spoken: DATS stores a date, year, month, day. TIMS stores a time, hours, minutes, seconds. CURR holds an amount. QUAN holds a quantity.

slides.label: WHY IT MATTERS
slides.heading: 100 of *what*?
slides.voiceover: An amount alone means nothing. A CURR field points to a CUKY field. That's the currency key, like INR or USD. A quantity works the same. A QUAN field points to a UNIT field.
slides.spoken: An amount alone means nothing. A CURR field points to a CUKY field. That's the currency key, like INR or USD. A quantity works the same. A QUAN field points to a UNIT field.

slides.label: REMEMBER
slides.heading: Use the type that *knows the value*
slides.body: Dates: DATS. Times: TIMS. Amounts: CURR + currency key. Quantities: QUAN + unit.
slides.voiceover: Takeaway: use the type that knows what the value means. Never CHAR eight for a date.
slides.spoken: Takeaway: use the type that knows what the value means. Never CHAR 8 for a date.

SAP domain, Part 6 of 12: data types for dates, times and money.

2. TIMS: a time (HHMMSS)
3. CURR: an amount that points to a currency key field (CUKY)
4. QUAN: a quantity that points to a unit field (UNIT)

slides.heading: *Output* Characteristics
slides.voiceover: The Format block says what's stored. Output Characteristics say how it's shown and typed. Output length is its width on screen. Separators count too.
slides.spoken: The Format block says what's stored. Output Characteristics say how it's shown and typed. Output length is its width on screen. Separators count too.

slides.heading: Four fields, *four jobs*
slides.voiceover: Conversion routine is where ALPHA lives. Sign allows negative values. Lower case keeps small letters as typed.
slides.spoken: Conversion routine is where ALPHA lives. Sign allows negative values. Lower case keeps small letters as typed.

slides.label: COMMON MISTAKE
slides.heading: A city named *Pune*
slides.voiceover: Common mistake: lower case off. Users type Pune, SAP saves PUNE. Tick lower case to keep it. Same for Sign: no tick, no minus.
slides.spoken: Common mistake: lower case off. Users type Pune, SAP saves PUNE. Tick lower case to keep it. Same for Sign: no tick, no minus.

slides.label: REMEMBER
slides.heading: Format = stored, Output = *shown*
slides.body: Format decides what is stored. Output Characteristics decide what the user sees and types.
slides.voiceover: Takeaway: format decides what's stored. Output decides what the user sees and types. Even a minus sign.
slides.spoken: Takeaway: format decides what's stored. Output decides what the user sees and types. Even a minus sign.

SAP domain, Part 7 of 12: Output Characteristics on the Definition tab.

1. Output Length: how many characters the field takes on screen, separators included
2. Convers. Routine: e.g. ALPHA adds and removes leading zeros
3. Sign: allows negative values
4. Lower Case: keeps small letters; otherwise screen input becomes upper case
